The 30-year, by a wide margin. At the same rate you carry a larger balance for twice as long. On $300k at 6%, the 15-year costs about $155k in interest (payment ≈ $2,531/month) versus about $347k for the 30-year (≈ $1,799/month). In practice 30-year rates are usually higher too, which widens the gap.

The tradeoff is the higher monthly payment on the 15-year. If you'd rather keep the 30-year's flexibility, extra principal payments cut the interest substantially.
